specials.name: Lumber Kings Home Opener
specials.blurb: Buffalo-plaid bunting on the rafters rail, a plaid scarf on Doris's mirror and the ceremonial puck drop by Ronnie Haverstock, who is always asked and always says yes. Old Pete polishes the Shed bell in the lobby where people can see. The marquee says BEAT THE MILL.
goes_well: the HOME scoreboard works (or Doreen's flip chart is up)
Ronnie drops the puck
the coffee machine flips to WORKING
a clean intermission flood under eight minutes
goes_badly: the roof drips on the home blue line
the beer licence isn't sorted
Kessler wins 5-3 again, like 1974

specials.name: Halloween Public Skate
specials.blurb: Pumpkins on the boards, costumes on the ice and Doris in a sheet as a ghost (Earl: 'Fine. Once.'). Dylan runs a haunted dressing room that is mostly him in a goalie mask saying 'boo'.
goes_well: dry ice in the rental line, not on the rink
candy at the skate rental window
Doris's ghost sheet stays on through the flood
goes_badly: slush and capes do not mix
the haunted dressing room makes Birdie cry
somebody's inflatable costume meets a skate blade

specials.name: Doris Day
specials.blurb: The rink and Doris both opened on Saturday 2 November 1974, so every 2 November the town wishes Doris a happy birthday. Earl allows a cake in the bay (not on her), kids sign a card taped to the snow tank, and Doris does a slow lap with her headlamps on while Doreen plays Happy Birthday in Organ 2.
goes_well: Doris starts first pull
Earl adds a tally mark with the whole town watching
the cake has her original cream and blue
goes_badly: Doris won't start (it's the plugs)
somebody mentions a Flatley
the cake ends up on the ice

specials.name: Valley Peewee Tournament
specials.rule: third weekend of November (and one weekend a month in winter)
specials.blurb: Teams from five towns, games every 75 minutes with a flood, hockey bags lining the corridor like sandbags and a schedule board on an easel that the owner updates live as the day runs late. The Hot Stove serves the Legion's tournament chili, Tommy Bellweather runs the crest-trading table like a bank, and Bob Ferreira, who chairs the committee, would like it to run on time for once in its life.
goes_well: the schedule runs within 30 minutes
the fries never run out
four usable dressing rooms
a Millbrook kid scores the winner on home ice
goes_badly: one long overtime pushes every game late
the fryer dies at 11 am
a rut at the blue line catches a Peewee's edge

specials.name: Skate with Santa
specials.blurb: Santa arrives on Doris, as every year, and Santa is Big Gord, shouting 'Ho ho ho, Big Gord won't let you walk!' from the snow tank. Earl drives. Doris wears felt antlers but not the red nose; if somebody adds the nose, Earl takes it off before every flood and puts it back after.
goes_well: the mitten tree in the lobby is full
Millbrook Elementary's paper snowflakes are on the glass
Santa does not fall (2011)
goes_badly: Santa falls (2011; it still got a 10)
the hot chocolate runs out
the red nose incident escalates

specials.name: The Snowflake Showcase
specials.blurb: The learn-to-skate kids and the figure club skate for their families under paper snowflakes hung from the rafters on fishing line. It is the night Maddie Pruitt lets go of the chair, if the season has gone right. Every parent has a phone up; Colette asks them to also hold a hand.
goes_well: minus three and a half at the surface
the music doesn't skip
every small skater gets a snowflake medal
Maddie lets go
goes_badly: hockey ruts left from the afternoon
a cold stands and a broken heater
the sound system plays the Kingsport dirge by mistake

specials.name: Haverstock Old-timers' Invitational
specials.blurb: One weekend in January, eighteen hours of old-timers' hockey, a beer garden in the hall and old team photos brought down from the walls and set on easels round the room with the 1994 Cup photo in the middle. Ronnie's daughter Tracy runs it; Ronnie is embarrassed by all of it. Barry Pomeroy turns up with a suitcase.
goes_well: a beer garden licence in hand
the dead spot behind the north net left alone
Ronnie scores off the bank and pretends it was luck
goes_badly: no licence, dry hall
somebody has 'fixed' the north boards
ambulance on standby, used

specials.name: Hockey Day in Millbrook
specials.blurb: One day, every level: Tiny Tykes at 7, minor hockey all morning, the Mallards at noon, the figure club's exhibition between periods, the Flood Crew against the Molars at 4 and the Lumber Kings at 7, with Bernie Szabo calling all of it on CKVL from a card table at the glass.
goes_well: every slot runs on time
Bernie's card table has a heater
the Lumber Kings win in front of the whole town
goes_badly: the plant trips at noon
the ice wears out by the Kings game
the canteen's out of everything by 3

specials.name: Millbrook Winter Carnival
specials.blurb: The town fair: an ice sculpture contest in the lot (the Flood Crew carves a Doris, the Molars carve a molar), King of Mount Doris for the kids, lanterns across the lot, a hot chocolate stand outside, a figure club exhibition under the coloured gels and, on Saturday night, the broomball final. The Clarion prints the sculpture results on page one.
goes_well: a cold, clear weekend so the sculptures last
the figure exhibition on figure ice
the broomball final on ice that won't eat sneakers
goes_badly: a February thaw melts the Doris sculpture
the plant struggles with the doors open all day
the Hot Stove runs out of hot chocolate by noon

specials.name: The Broomball Beer Cup (Carnival Final)
specials.blurb: The Carnival's Saturday night broomball final: the Harlow Falls Broomball Club and anyone with sneakers and a grudge, with the beer garden open in the hall. The trophy is the Golden Boot, a rubber boot painted gold, which lives on Rhonda Pelkey's porch because nobody has given it a better home.
goes_well: the boards edged and the flood done an hour before, not a minute before
nachos at the Hot Stove
the Golden Boot gets a place in the trophy case
goes_badly: the ice is wet and nobody can stand
a hockey team books over it
the noise complaint from Church Street

specials.name: Valentine's Couples Skate
specials.blurb: The lights go down, Doreen plays love songs on the Casio in Organ 2 and couples go round holding hands, or holding each other up. The Hot Stove sells The Haverstock in pairs. Every year somebody proposes; this year Devon Marsh has been checking his coat pocket since January.
goes_well: the lights dim and the ice is smooth
Doreen takes requests
Devon doesn't fall at the key moment
goes_badly: slush ruins the romance
the heater is broken in the stands
Devon falls at the key moment (still a yes)

specials.name: Harold Penner Night
specials.blurb: A Lumber Kings home game in the name of Mayor Harold Penner, who cut the ribbon in 1974 and shouted 'SKATE!' from seat C-4-7 for thirty years. The Kings wear the 1974 socks, which smell like 1974. His granddaughter June sits in his seat and leads the whole building in the shout every time someone stops moving.
goes_well: seat C-4-7 is cleaned and the plaque polished
the whole building shouts SKATE together
the Kings win in the 1974 socks
goes_badly: somebody sits in C-4-7
the HOME scoreboard is still dead for the man who opened the rink
ice under 60 on his night

specials.name: Figure Club Test Day
specials.blurb: Madame Lacombe drives two hours from Sainte-Odile with her own blanket to evaluate the club's skaters on skills, dances and free skate; this year Josée Thibodeau tests her Senior Bronze freeskate and wants the ice fresh, flat and fair. Parents whisper in the stands, skaters wait in the lobby in warm-ups and the judges' box is either warm or a disaster.
goes_well: a heater in the judges' box
minus four at the surface and no ruts
silence during the tests
coffee for the panel
goes_badly: a cold judges' box (she remembers)
the goal horn goes off by accident
a stick and puck group booked into the lobby

specials.name: Learn-to-Skate Graduation
specials.blurb: Week ten of the adult and kids' learn-to-skate: everyone skates one lap without the boards, demonstrates a stop (any stop) and gets a certificate in one of Penny's very good cards, signed by Penny, Colette and, if she can be talked into it, Bev. Gary Pruett comes back to stop in front of the bench, as an alumnus.
goes_well: rental skates sharpened that week
families in the stands
Walter and Marisol both let go of the boards
goes_badly: blunt rentals (number 41)
a hockey session overruns into it
nobody can stop and the boards take a beating

specials.name: The Spring Carnival (the ice show)
specials.blurb: The Millbrook Figure Skating Club's annual carnival, its fifty-first, before the ice comes out: Gus's coloured gels on the lamps (pink, blue, amber and one green nobody likes), the 50 Carnivals banner lowered to just above the ice, themed numbers, the little ones in costumes made by their parents and a finale where every skater, coach and willing hockey player does one lap together. Earl does the last flood of the season straight after, and the town watches that too.
goes_well: the gels found and the lamps safe to dress
ice rated 75 or better
Josée lands the double axel
Earl's last flood gets applause
goes_badly: the roof drips on the finale (it is March weather)
the ice is soft by the second act
the plant is shut early to save power

specials.name: Doris's Retirement Fund Skate-a-thon
specials.blurb: Twelve hours of pledged laps for the pickle jar labelled DORIS RETIREMENT FUND, which Earl says is pointless because she is not retiring. Dylan counts the laps, Irene skates the most, and Earl refuses to attend, then turns up at 6 pm and drives the last flood.
goes_well: the ice holds up for twelve hours
the pickle jar passes $1,000
Earl turns up
goes_badly: the ice is slush by 3 pm
nobody brings pledge sheets
Earl hears the word 'retirement' once too often
